                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question">Your institution has a strategy and an overarching structure supporting internationalisation</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The internationalisation strategy is available and prominently displayed on your website</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Internationalisation is an important driver for institutional change, and has a great influence on the major activities of a higher education institution (HEI) i.e. education and research. The importance of internationalisation is recognised, and most institutions have a strategy for internationalisation. However, for a strategy to be efficient, and for it to drive the HEI's activities regarding internationalisation, there is a need for its acceptance from across the whole institution. In addition the strategy could also be accessible to external collaborative partners. It is highly important to have the institution's internationalisation and modernisation strategy published and easily accessible to all.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution has a clear plan to implement the strategy</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The strategy and policy should include explicit allocation of responsibilities for its efficient implementation to individuals at all levels of the institution, from senior management to the heads of departments, schools and faculties, to academic and administrative staff. This will ensure acceptance and accountability for the strategy. The internationalisation strategy and policy should outline a specific implementation plan that sets out explicitly the financial and human resources available.&nbsp; For example, it is recommended to set up an International Relations Office (IRO) to implement mobility and other international projects.</p><p>As with any other activity, the institutional implementation of the internationalisation strategy is dependent on the people behind the activities. It is highly important for an institution to have staff with the right set of skills and knowledge driving the internationalisation agenda and liaising with international students and staff members. Therefore understanding the development needs of the staff and supporting their professional development should be a high priority for the institution. Such development should focus on both staff engaged in international activities as well as the supporting staff, ensuring the most efficient implementation of international activities and cooperative projects across the institution. For example, trainings/webinars/projects could be organised on intercultural competences and communication, project management, enhancement of internationalisation at home/intercultural, or other activities suggested by the staff and supported by the hierarchy.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It promotes incoming and outgoing student and staff mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobility is important to the development of the institution as a whole as well as for the individual participants. Therefore the HEI should make mobility and international cooperation a central element in its institutional policies, and explicitly and consistently promote and support student and staff mobility. Non-discrimination policies and further emphasis on the promotion of mobility for under-represented groups should also form an integral part of the institutional support structures.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It promotes engagement in European and international cooperation projects</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution's internationalisation strategy and policy should explicitly and consistently promote the development of cooperation with partners in other EU and non-EU countries. The activities and co-operation projects agreed by the HEI should be based on identified needs. In addition they should identify geographical and subject priorities of the internationalisation strategy.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The implementation of the strategic plan is monitored</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>International activity, including co-operation projects and mobility should be carefully monitored. Clear and unambiguous monitoring of such activity are key to ensuring success. Explicit indicators should be developed to show specific success scenarios. The indicators should be SMART.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Incentives are provided to staff involved in international activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in such international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI. It should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation. As part of the institutional modernisation and internationalisation strategy, concrete support measures should be defined at both institutional and departmental levels to encourage and recognise staff participating in such projects, as well as allow adequate time to carry out this work.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">

                        <div class="eche-officer-question">Your institution has established a framework of Inter-Institutional Agreements for Erasmus+ mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">They are based on areas of mutual interest</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is vital that Inter-Institutional Agreements are based on areas of mutual interest. These agreements should identify shared quality requirements specific to the planned exchanges, including concrete proposals as to how these activities will contribute to the development of learning and teaching in participating institutions. The involvement of academic staff is key to ensuring that the selection of partners is based on sufficient knowledge of the area. Each HEI should decide who is responsible for initiating, signing and implementing these agreements and the list of responsible persons should be available on the website for contact and consultation purposes.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">They are based on the compatibility of study programmes</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Inter-Institutional Agreements should be based on a comprehensive understanding of the partner HEIs, the compatibility of study programmes, quality levels and standards considered adequate for student and staff mobility activities. For example, selected partners should have learning, teaching and assessment procedures that can be accepted by the sending institution without requiring mobile students to do any additional work or take examinations upon returning from the receiving institution. The compatibility of the programmes should be reflected in the learning outcomes to be achieved.</p>                      </div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question">Your institution expresses its commitment to equal access and opportunities to mobile participants</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">There are specific provisions e.g. in the general policies, rules and regulations of the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>In signing the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education, the institution agrees to respect <strong>in full</strong> the principles of non-discrimination as set out in the Programme. The institution must clearly demonstrate through its policies, rules and regulations that equal access and opportunities to mobile participants from all backgrounds. Which means that all individuals or groups will be treated equally, irrespective of their characteristics. In accordance with Article 21 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, there should be no discrimination "based on sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation". For more information, see: <a href="http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf">http://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The principle - that extra fees are not being charged to incoming mobile students - is implemented</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The receiving institution must <strong>not </strong>charge any type of fees to incoming mobility students for the tuition, registration or examination of these students or for their access to laboratory, library and other facilities offered to local students.<br>In certain cases, however, mobile students may be required to pay small fees for insurance, student unions, use of miscellaneous materials (e.g. photocopies, laboratory products) on the same basis as these are charged to local students. Students should be made aware of these extra costs before the start of mobility. Fees may only be charged in the case of full degree mobility or for students registered in joint degree programmes.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All students and staff (incoming and outgoing) are treated equally in all academic and service matters</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>In accordance with equal access and opportunities, all students and staff should be treated equally in all academic and service matters. Clear appeal procedures should be in place to ensure equal treatment. There should be individuals - such as mentors and counsellors - available to offer support.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It provides incoming mobile participants with access to the same services and facilities available to local students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is vital to ensure that incoming mobility participants have full access to the same services and facilities as local students and staff. For example, mobility participants with special needs can benefit from the support services that the receiving institution offers to its local students and staff.</p>                      </div>

                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Ensuring that the mobile participant, sending and receiving HEI/organisation/enterprise (i.e. all three parties) sign the Learning Agreement before the start of the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The purpose of the Learning Agreement is to provide a transparent and efficient preparation of the study period abroad and to ensure that the student will receive recognition in his/her degree for the educational components or traineeship successfully completed abroad. The Learning Agreement:</p><ul><li>Sets out the learning outcomes for the mobility, including both the educational components or traineeship activities to be carried out by the student at the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise, which will be recognised by the sending institution upon successful completion of the study programme abroad and counted towards his/her degree.</li><li>Ensures full recognition for satisfactorily completed activities of study mobility and traineeships in terms of credits awarded, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams, and documents these credits in the student records, so that they can be identified in a transparent way.</li></ul><p>The Learning Agreement is binding for all parties and constitutes the cornerstone of successful student mobility (for studies, traineeships, and combinations thereof), including quality assurances and the process for transparent transfer of credits. Therefore, it is essential to conduct mobility based on an agreed and signed Learning Agreement. The Learning Agreement should be agreed and signed by all parties (the student, the sending institution and the receiving institution/organisation/enterprise) before the start of the mobility. It is not compulsory to circulate papers with original signatures; scanned copies of signatures or digital signatures may be accepted, depending on the national legislation.</p><p>The EU official templates for Learning Agreements for studies and traineeships are available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm&nbsp;&nbsp;</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Including allocation of responsibility to an academic who has the authority to approve, amend and recognise the Learning Agreements on behalf of the responsible academic body</span>

                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution appoints responsible person(s) to deal with practical issues (e.g. social, health, and/or psychological problems)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution should ensure there are named, visible persons who are responsible for the practical issues associated with integrating mobile students. This visibility should be ensured through introduction to this function during the Welcome / Orientation period and be detailed on the website so all mobile students can easily access this support, throughout their stay.&nbsp;</p><p>Non-academic mentoring and support arrangements should already be outlined in the Course Catalogue of the receiving HEI, in the section on general information for students, with relevant contact persons in the respective areas. Academic advisors should have close contact with the practical services which are available to incoming participants as they are often the first line of contact to the incoming student. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>

                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>

                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>

Unser Ziel ist eine Solaranlage auf jedem Dach, ein Speicher in jedem Haus und ein E-Auto in jeder Garage. Enpal macht das m\u00f6glich mit einer integrierten Gesamtl\u00f6sung f\u00fcr dezentrale Energie \u2013 von Solaranlage und Batteriespeicher \u00fcber Wallbox, Smart Meter bis zur W\u00e4rmepumpe. Herzst\u00fcck ist unsere KI-gest\u00fctzte Plattform Enpal.One<\/a>+, die tausende Systeme intelligent vernetzt und Strombezug sowie -einspeisung effizient am Energiemarkt optimiert.<\/p>

metrify ist die Smart-Metering-Unit von Enpal und die digitale Infrastruktur f\u00fcr ein intelligentes Energie-\u00d6kosystem. Mit zehntausenden installierten iMSys und skalierbaren Prozessen machen wir Energie messbar, steuerbar und wirtschaftlich nutzbar \u2013 und schaffen gemeinsam mit Partnern die Basis f\u00fcr neue Gesch\u00e4ftsmodelle der Energiewende.<\/p>

<\/h3>

Deine Aufgaben<\/h3>

  • Du betreust operative Prozesse rund um Mieterstrom und stellst sicher, dass Vorg\u00e4nge vollst\u00e4ndig, korrekt und fristgerecht bearbeitet werden.<\/p><\/li>

  • Du arbeitest eng mit Marktpartnern, externen Dienstleistern und internen Teams zusammen und koordinierst Abstimmungen per E-Mail, Telefon, Portalen und Tickets.<\/p><\/li>

  • Du begleitest die Einf\u00fchrung und Weiterentwicklung neuer Prozesse gemeinsam mit externen und internen Stakeholdern.<\/p><\/li>

  • Du \u00fcbernimmst Verantwortung f\u00fcr kleinere Projekte und Prozessinitiativen und steuerst diese von der Abstimmung bis zur Umsetzung.<\/p><\/li>

  • Du arbeitest t\u00e4glich mit technischen Systemen und unterschiedlichen Tools, verstehst deren Zusammenh\u00e4nge und stellst sicher, dass Prozesse darin korrekt abgebildet werden.<\/p><\/li>

  • Du erkennst Abweichungen, Prozessfehler und Verbesserungspotenziale, analysierst Ursachen und entwickelst pragmatische L\u00f6sungen.<\/p><\/li>

  • Du beh\u00e4ltst auch bei mehreren parallelen Themen den \u00dcberblick, setzt Priorit\u00e4ten und sorgst f\u00fcr eine strukturierte Umsetzung.<\/p><\/li>

  • Du unterst\u00fctzt dabei, Prozesse skalierbarer, effizienter und transparenter zu gestalten.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

    <\/p>

    Dein Profil<\/h3>

    • Du hast Interesse an operativen Prozessen, Projektmanagement und der Zusammenarbeit mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern.<\/p><\/li>

    • Du arbeitest strukturiert, analytisch und l\u00f6sungsorientiert und kannst komplexe Abl\u00e4ufe schnell erfassen.<\/p><\/li>

    • Du hast eine hohe Affinit\u00e4t zu digitalen und technischen Systemen und findest dich schnell in neuen Tools und Prozessen zurecht.<\/p><\/li>

    • Du kommunizierst klar und verbindlich und f\u00fchlst dich in der Zusammenarbeit mit externen Partnern und internen Teams wohl.<\/p><\/li>

    • Du kannst mehrere Themen gleichzeitig koordinieren, sinnvoll priorisieren und selbstst\u00e4ndig vorantreiben.<\/p><\/li>

    • Du hinterfragst bestehende Abl\u00e4ufe und bringst eigene Ideen f\u00fcr Prozessverbesserungen und pragmatische L\u00f6sungen ein.<\/p><\/li>

    • Erste Erfahrung in Operations, Projektmanagement, Prozessmanagement oder Energiewirtschaft ist von Vorteil, aber kein Muss.<\/p><\/li>

    • Du hast Lust, dich in das Themenfeld Mieterstrom und energiewirtschaftliche Marktprozesse einzuarbeiten.<\/p><\/li>

    • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

      <\/p>

      Du bist interessiert, auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen erf\u00fcllst? Bewirb dich trotzdem! Wir freuen uns darauf, dein Potenzial zu entdecken - unabh\u00e4ngig davon, ob deine Erfahrung jede einzelne Voraussetzung erf\u00fcllt. \u2600\ufe0f<\/p>

      <\/p>

      Darauf kannst Du Dich freuen<\/strong><\/h3>

      • Arbeite in Deutschlands erstem gr\u00fcnen Unicorn<\/strong> - Gestalte aktiv die solare Energiewende mit.<\/p><\/li>

      • Die Sonne scheint auf der ganzen Welt<\/strong> - Bei Enpal arbeitest du mit einem hochmotivierten, diversen Team aus \u00fcber 65 Nationalit\u00e4ten.<\/p><\/li>

      • Das ideale Setup f\u00fcr deinen Fokus - <\/strong>Wir sind \u00fcberzeugt, dass exzellente Ergebnisse dort entstehen, wo die Bedingungen stimmen. Deshalb setzen wir auf ein hybrides Arbeitskonzept, das dir die Freiheit gibt, immer genau so zu arbeiten, wie es am besten zu deinen Aufgaben passt. Du brauchst neue Impulse auf internationalem Niveau? Mit Workflex bieten wir, abh\u00e4ngig von deiner Verantwortung, die M\u00f6glichkeit, deine T\u00e4tigkeit bis zu 30 Tage im Jahr ins Ausland zu verlegen.<\/p><\/li>

      • Grown-up Business & Startup Spirit<\/strong> - In unserem modernen Office in Berlin-Friedrichshain findest du von h\u00f6henverstellbaren Tischen, Tischtennisplatte bis gef\u00fcllten Getr\u00e4nkek\u00fchlschr\u00e4nken und Barista-Coffee alles was das Herz begehrt.<\/p><\/li>

      • Dein Kick-start bei Enpal<\/strong> - Onboarding-Tag mit Welcome Bag, Buddy-Programm und einem Team, das dich wirklich abholt.<\/p><\/li>

      • Bleib auf dem Laufenden & gestalte mit<\/strong> - <\/strong>Transparente All-Hands, kurze Entscheidungswege und eine offene Feedback-Kultur, denn ohne Fehler gibt es keinen Fortschritt.<\/p><\/li>

      • Energiewende geht nur gemeinsam<\/strong> - Bei Enpal erwartet dich ein legend\u00e4rer Teamspirit und unvergessliche Team- und Companyevents.<\/p><\/li>

        <\/p>

Nice to have

Terms

  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

MoneyHero Group (MHG) is hiring a Product Design Lead who is an equal parts product thinker, systems designer, and AI-powered creator. You’ll shape intuitive, high-performing experiences that help millions across Singapore, Hong Kong, the Philippines, and Taiwan make smarter financial decisions.

As part of a lean, high-velocity design team, you won’t just design interfaces - you’ll shape product strategy, challenge assumptions, and use AI tools to supercharge how fast we ideate, validate, and ship. You’ll move fluidly between deep product work and rapid campaign execution, bringing first-principles thinking and an obsession with user outcomes to every problem.

Product Design & Execution:

  • Design for conversion across both core product flows and growth surfaces = campaign pages, microsites, and high-impact landing experiences.
  • Apply and evolve our Figma design system, ensuring consistency, accessibility, and scalability across platforms.
  • Integrate insights from analytics, experimentation, and user feedback to iterate and continuously improve user journeys.
  • Partner closely with engineers to ensure design intent carries through implementation and contribute to QA when needed.
  • Introduce, champion, and document AI-accelerated design practices to help the team work smarter, faster, and with higher quality.

Leadership & People Management:

  • Lead and inspire a small team of 2 Product Designers, providing the mentorship and guidance necessary to elevate their technical skills and creative thinking.
  • Deliver clear, actionable feedback and coach team members on how to navigate complex stakeholder requirements without compromising on design quality.

  • Establish high standards for design output by empowering the team to deliver user-centric solutions that meet both business goals and technical constraints.
  • Act as a core thought partner to senior leadership across Product, Data, and Engineering to bridge the gap between user experience and technical feasibility.

  • 7+ years of experience in UX/UI or product design, with a portfolio showcasing both product features and marketing or growth work.
  • 2–3 years of leadership experience in leading design initiatives or small teams.
  • Proficient in Figma, with experience working with component libraries and modern design systems.
  • Strong understanding of interaction design, responsive layouts, and UX best practices.
  • Comfortable using AI tools as core extensions of your workflow, from ideation to production.
  • Bonus: Working knowledge of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, or familiarity with engineering workflows.
  • Fluent in English; Mandarin or Cantonese is a plus.

You’ll fit right if you have:

  • A strong product mindset and a bias toward shipping meaningful impact—not just making screens look good.
  • A first-principles approach to problem-solving and the ability to influence PMs and stakeholders through clear reasoning, structured thinking, and evidence-backed design decisions.
  • Experience designing high-conversion, consumer-facing web or mobile experiences.
  • Comfort context-switching between deep product work and fast-turnaround campaign or growth projects.
  • Natural curiosity and enthusiasm for pushing the boundaries of what AI can enable in modern product design.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills - especially when working with remote and cross-functional teams.

#MoneyHeroGroup

This position defines and implements RFP requirements and manages the proposal life cycle process (RFP to Proposal to Award to Project Handoff) and associated deliverables to ensure internal and customer proposal requirements are completed on time. This position will require strong people management skills to manage a medium-to-large-sized team of employees as direct reports.

The Senior Proposal Manager may also be responsible for leading the interface with various internal and external stakeholders on bid proposal and project planning teams, communicating and presenting effectively and with influence to the client group and team members. They will provide technical guidance to less experienced personnel and will act as a manager of the process.

Ensure that team goals, roles, protocols, and business relationships are consistent with high-performance requirements and congruent with the company's strategy. Manages in an environment of trust and candor, promotes accountability, and assertively offers encouragement and constructive feedback.

  • Oversees a team, including proposal administrator, bid coordinator, technical writers, and non-people-manager technical proposal managers.
  • Fully understands the major business components and implications specific to H&M West's pricing and proposal strategies.
  • Ensure compliance with the Henkels & McCoy West established Project Management Methodology and upholds H&M West safety and quality management protocols.
  • Support the Project and Business Development teams by executing bid, pricing, and proposal strategies.
  • Manage multiple deadlines and documents while still meeting client qualifications and deadlines.
  • Read compliance requirements and create a document that is organized logically and meets client requests.
  • Define and implement RFP requirements. Manages the proposal life cycle process (RFP to Proposal to Award to Project Handoff) and associated deliverables to ensure internal and customer proposal requirements are completed on time.
  • Support the Project and Business Development teams by executing bid, pricing, and proposal strategies.
  • Assess internal pricing strategies and performance against service delivery goals.
  • Write sections of documents as necessary.
  • Apply company branding and style guidelines to documents, ensuring multiple documents have one Voice, as well as consistent language and message.
  • Work closely with different teams to convey requirements, ensuring accountability for deliverables to keep proposals on schedule and compliant.
  • Skilled in using Microsoft Word, Excel, and Adobe Acrobat.
  • Knowledge of Procore, B2W, and P6 a plus.

Qualifications

  • Ability to write clearly and concisely.
  • Experience as a proposal coordinator, technical writer, or similar in the AEC industry, preferably with a contractor involved in EPC or Design-Build alternative delivery methods.
  • Experience with and knowledge of subcontractor bidding events.
  • Proven excellence in technical writing and organization.
  • Ability to collect and organize large amounts of information efficiently and promptly.
  • Solid computer skills and proficiency in MS Office applications.
  • Proven experience as a leader with a team of direct reports, especially in the construction arena.
  • Moderately complex problem-solving skills and proactive motivation to use critical thinking skills.

Educational Background:

Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communications, English, or similar and/or technical writing certificate with equivalent years of experience.

Years of Relevant Experience:

7-10 years of relevant experience; 5+ years of leadership experience mentoring & developing a team of technical writers

Henkels & McCoy West is an Equal Opportunity Employer of Minorities, Females, Protected Veterans, and Individuals with Disabilities.

Position Description

The Solution Architect is a senior, customer-facing leader with a deep background in Pharmaceutical Regulatory who owns the full post-sale journey for Kivo’s customers. The primary focus of this role is driving customer outcomes, retention, and expansion through proactive success management that starts with leading hands-on implementation projects and continues through to Customer Success interactions. You will build deep, trusted relationships with Kivo’s customers, lead implementations that set customers up for long-term success and serve as their strategic partner throughout their time with Kivo. This role thrives at the intersection of strategic account management and operational delivery in regulated environments. While primarily US-focused, the role may require occasional time-shifting to support EU-based implementation projects and customers.

Key Responsibilities

Implementation Consulting

Working in partnership with Kivo’s US based implementation team:

  • Solution Design: Engage early in the sales process to assist with the definition of requirements and project scoping
  • Deliver implementations: Lead end-to-end implementations of the Kivo platform through structured project management, and governance.
  • Design & configure: Facilitate discovery and design workshops; translate regulated process requirements (GxP, 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11) into configured platform solutions with documented decisions and guide the adoption of Kivo.
  • Support validation: Support the customer’s validation workstream by educating customers in the Kivo validation methodology and providing an orientation to Kivo documentation.
  • Support data migration: Partner with the Data Migration team on discovery, field mapping, dry-run coordination, and production cutover checklists for compliant data transfers.
  • Enable go-live: Guide customers through change management activities: defect triage, go-live readiness assessments, user training enablement, and post-go-live stabilization.

Customer Success

Working in partnership with the VP, Services:

  • Own account health: Manage a portfolio of NA accounts as the primary strategic point of contact post-implementation
  • Drive outcomes and expansion: Build and maintain tailored success plans aligned to each customer’s business goals; partner with Sales to identify, qualify, and advance expansion and upsell opportunities within your portfolio.
  • Executive alignment: Cultivate senior-level relationships within customer organizations; deliver executive-ready insights, business reviews, and ROI narratives that reinforce Kivo’s value.
  • Champion the customer: Serve as the primary voice of Kivo customers to the internal team—surface product feedback, advocate for roadmap priorities, and collaborate with Product on features and packaged offerings that reflect NA market needs.
  • Manage upgrades and adoption: Proactively manage customers through new feature releases and configuration changes, ensuring smooth adoption and building internal champions who drive platform utilization.
  • Retain and grow the base: Own GRR and NRR metrics for your portfolio; develop and execute playbooks for at-risk accounts, renewals, and expansion conversations in coordination with Sales leadership.

What You’ve Done

Required

  • 5–10+ years of experience in a customer success, implementation, or blended services role (e.g. Delivery Lead) within a life-sciences SaaS environment (pharma, biotech, med-device, or CRO).
  • Strong domain knowledge in Regulatory Affairs or Operations for pharmaceutical/biotech or medtech industries is a must
  • Demonstrated track record managing across a portfolio of accounts.
  • Working knowledge of regulated industry requirements (GxP, 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11) and comfort supporting validation deliverables (CSA/CSV).
  • Experience leading software implementations in a regulated environment, including project planning, stakeholder management, and go-live delivery.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; comfortable presenting to technical users and C-suite stakeholders alike.
  • Based in the US with the flexibility to occasionally time-shift for EU-based project collaboration.
  • Applied AI experience with AI models (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot) to build workflows, automations, or skills and the ability to guide customers in their use - not just as an end user

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience with life-sciences SaaS platforms such as Vault (Quality/RIM/Clinical), MasterControl, TrackWise/ETQ, or comparable eQMS, eTMF, or RIM systems.
  • Prior experience working in hyper-growth, fast-paced environments and managing multiple priorities
  • PMP, Agile/Scrum certification, or equivalent project management training.

Who You Are

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent experience.
  • Drive: The ability and desire to work in a fast-paced environment and manage shifting priorities and maintain a balance outside the office, this is not 9/9/6.
  • Curiosity: Systems thinking mindset, and a curiosity to learn and understand the “why”
  • Work Ethic: A focus and commitment to customer success

      <title>Stripe: Abuse Research Engineer</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote from the US
</p>

<h2>Who we are</h2>
<h3>About Stripe</h3>
<p><span>Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.</span></p>
<h3>About the team</h3>
<p>Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.</p>
<h2>What you’ll do</h2>
<p>As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. &nbsp;Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. &nbsp;Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.</p>
<h3>Responsibilities</h3>
<ul>
<li>Proactive Threat Hunting &amp; Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.</li>
<li>FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints. &nbsp;</li>
<li>Threat Intelligence &amp; Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows. &nbsp;</li>
<li>Cross-Functional Advisories &amp; Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security. &nbsp;</li>
<li>Agentic Testing &amp; Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls. &nbsp;</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>Who you are</strong></h2>
<p><span>We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.</span></p>
<h3>Minimum requirements</h3>
<ul>
<li>5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation methodologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>Strong communication skills with a proven ability to translate complex technical research into clear, actionable recommendations and advisories for cross-functional partners.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Preferred qualifications</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>Deep technical understanding of threat actor motivations, infrastructure, and TTPs specific to financial fraud (e.g., ATO, Card Testing, Credential Stuffing).&nbsp;</li>
<li>Familiarity with standardized taxonomies such as FT3 or MITRE ATT&amp;CK.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>Proficiency with engineering, data processing, and analysis platforms such as Databricks, Trino, PySpark, Pandas, or Scikit-Learn.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>Proven background utilizing Threat Intelligence Platforms (TIPs), tactical threat feeds, OSINT, and breach intelligence.&nbsp;</li>
<li>Demonstrated capability building or leveraging agentic LLM tools, automated testing systems, or control validation frameworks to model adversary behavior at scale.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li>
<li>Participation in industry conferences, webinars, or threat-sharing groups, alongside relevant professional certifications (e.g., GCTI, GCFA, OSCP).</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/stripe-abuse-research-engineer">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/stripe-abuse-research-engineer</a></p>
</description>

      <title>Doximity: Commercial Data Scientist</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> San Francisco, CA or Remote (U.S.)
</p>

<h3><strong>Commercial Data Scientist</strong></h3>
<p>Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients.&nbsp;</p>
<p>At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.</p>
<p><br><em>This role can be filled in the Northeast (New York, NJ, Philadelphia, Boston), our San Francisco headquarters, OR other remote locations in the U.S.</em></p>
<p><strong>As a Commercial Data Scientist</strong>, you’ll work within cross-functional delivery teams alongside other analysts, engineers, and commercial stakeholders in discovering data insights to help improve healthcare.</p>
<p><strong>How you’ll make an impact:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Deliver novel and impactful insights for client organizations using machine learning and AI technologies.</li>
<li>Work closely with our Product, Platform Data, Insights &amp; Strategy, and Sales teams to create client-facing analyses.</li>
<li>Showcase your engineering skills by creating data products from scratch and automating code so they can be re-used by other teammates and future projects.</li>
<li>Leverage Doximity's extensive datasets to identify and classify behavioral patterns of medical professionals on our platform.</li>
<li>Embrace the challenge of a fast-paced environment to exceed client expectations</li>
</ul>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>The Core Values of the Client Intelligence team</strong></p>
<p><strong>As an organization we value diversity - </strong>in backgrounds and in experiences. Healthcare is a universal concern, and we need people from all backgrounds to help build a better future for all. Below are additional core values specific to the Insights Team.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Collaboration</strong>—The best candidates and teammates are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.</li>
<li><strong>Passion for Data</strong>—You’re going to help our clients and team members with data-driven decision making. We need someone that can manipulate millions of rows of data and also ask the right questions to find the important insights.</li>
<li><strong>Reliability</strong> – Our team is efficient, flexible, and agile only because we trust the reliability of each member. We need self-starters and goal-oriented individuals for our continued success.</li>
<li><strong>Curiosity</strong> – Continuous learning is a cornerstone at Doximity, and curious individuals thrive in our environment. We’re looking for someone who is curious enough about data to go above-and-beyond the task for the true insight.</li>
<li><strong>Respect</strong> – A key dynamic that allows our team to flourish is respect: for ourselves and our quality of work, for our teammates, and for our internal clients who are under the pressure of deadlines and finance goals.</li>
</ul>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>About you:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>At least <strong>4 years</strong> of professional experience as a Data Scientist or other related roles working with complex, high-volume, structured and unstructured datasets.</li>
<li>Prior experience in a data science consulting role at firms such as ZS, Trinity, IQVIA, BlueMatter, etc., where you thrived in a fast-paced environment</li>
<li>Advanced knowledge of statistical concepts — particularly exploratory data analysis, experimental design, and probability theory.</li>
<li>Deep understanding of modern machine learning techniques</li>
<li>Proven ability to design, train, and evaluate large-scale production models using frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.</li>
<li>Advanced SQL proficiency — skilled at writing and optimizing complex queries across multiple tables and data relationships.</li>
<li>Advanced Python skills, including understanding of object-oriented programming, production-grade code design, and modern data science libraries.</li>
<li>Hands-on experience with distributed data processing tools and concepts for scalable analysis and model training.</li>
<li>Excellent data visualization and storytelling abilities, with the capacity to translate technical insights into clear, compelling narratives for internal and client stakeholders.</li>
<li>Curious, fast learner with a demonstrated passion for data, continuous learning, and staying current with advances in machine learning research.</li>
</ul>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Fun</strong> <strong>Facts About the Client Intelligence team</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>We have access to one of the richest healthcare datasets in the world, with deep information on hundreds of thousands of clinicians and their connections.</li>
<li>Business decisions at Doximity are driven by our data, analyses, and insights.</li>
<li>The members of our team bring a diverse set of technical and cultural backgrounds.</li>
<li>We like to have fun - company outings, team lunches, and other social events!</li>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Compensation</strong></p>
<p>The anticipated total compensation for this role is $119,333 - $172,800 depending on factors such as experience, skills, location, and internal equity.</p>
<p>Our total compensation package may include:</p>

<li>Equity (where applicable)</li>

<p>Specific compensation details will be discussed during the interview process.</p>
<p>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Benefits</strong></p>
<p>In addition to competitive compensation, Doximity offers a comprehensive benefits package for full time employees. Some of our offerings include:</p>

<li>401(k) with company match</li>
